modules.summary: pans — five progressive tiers of training-data preprocessing.

api.name: Pan
api.doc: Abstract pan. Subclasses override :meth:`cook` (one line in, zero-or-one line out) or :meth:`iter` (full iterator override).

methods.name: cook
methods.signature: def cookself, line: str -> str | None

api.name: FryingPan
api.doc: Lightest tier. Strip trailing whitespace, pass everything else through. Useful when the input is already clean (already-formatted corpora, pre-tokenized chunks).

methods.name: cook
methods.signature: def cookself, line: str -> str | None

api.name: SaucePan
api.doc: Reduce. Collapse runs of internal whitespace, drop empty lines, strip leading/trailing whitespace. Standard mild cleaning for scraped or OCR'd text.

methods.name: cook
methods.signature: def cookself, line: str -> str | None

api.name: Skillet
api.doc: Versatile. Applies chat / instruction formatting by wrapping each line with role tags. ``mode='chat'`` yields ``<USER>line\n<ASSISTANT>`` templates; ``mode='instruct'`` yields ``### Instruction: line\n### Response:`` — use one when every input line is a user turn and the dataset is paired with assistant replies on the following line (or in a separate corpus).

methods.name: cook
methods.signature: def cookself, line: str -> str | None

api.name: GrillPan
api.doc: High direct heat. SaucePan-style cleaning plus deduplication (SHA1 hash set) and a minimum length filter. Safe on arbitrary web-scraped text: collapses boilerplate, drops single-word lines.

methods.name: cook
methods.signature: def cookself, line: str -> str | None

api.name: Wok
api.doc: Heaviest. Buffers the whole source in memory, shuffles it, and optionally injects line-reversal augmentation (``reverse_ratio`` fraction of lines emitted in reverse word order). Use this for small corpora where order-randomization matters and you can afford the memory.

api.name: pick_pan
api.signature: def pick_pantier: str, source: Path | str | Iterable[str], **kwargs: Any -> Pan

api.doc: Random word masking at ``rate``. Replaces whole whitespace- separated tokens with ``mask_token``.

api.name: Dish
api.doc: Typo injection. For each word with probability ``rate``, either drops a random internal character or duplicates one. Preserves first and last characters so words remain recognisable (the classic "jumbled letters still readable" effect).

api.name: TallHandmade
api.doc: Negation injection. Prepends ``negator`` ("NOT " by default) to a random token at ``rate``. Useful for hard-negative mining and negation-robust classifier training.

modules.summary: salt_shaker — gentle noise / data augmentation.

api.name: Shaker
api.doc: Abstract seasoning applicator. Subclasses override :meth:`season`.

api.name: FromTheBag
api.doc: Cheapest tier. Per-character substitution at ``rate`` with a random printable ASCII character. Preserves line length.

api.name: HandCrusher
api.doc: Middle tier. Token-level adjacent-swap at ``rate``. Produces lines that are still mostly readable but structurally shuffled.

api.name: PoshSaltDish
api.doc: Finest tier. Word-aware drop / duplicate / swap at independent rates. Keeps attached punctuation with its neighbour so commas and periods don't end up orphaned.

examples.title: Download, convert, and quantize
examples.description: The public convenience API used by the bundled quickstart example.
examples.code:
from pathlib import Path
from hypernix import convert_to_gguf, download_model, quantize_gguf

model_dir = download_model("hyper-Nix.2")
out = Path("./hypernix-gguf")
fp16 = convert_to_gguf(model_dir, out / "hypernix-fp16.gguf", dtype="fp16")
quantize_gguf(fp16, out / "hypernix-q4_k_m.gguf", "Q4_K_M")

examples.title: Use the multi-turn chat surface
examples.description: Create a session around an oven, then persist it when the workflow finishes.
examples.code:
from hypernix.countertop import Countertop
from hypernix.old_oven import preheat

oven = preheat("hyper-Nix.2")
chat = Countertop(oven, system="Answer with concise Python examples.")
print(chat.say("Show me a dataclass with validation."))
chat.save("session.json")

examples.title: Build a training framework
examples.description: Construct a framework, build its module, move it to a device, and save weights.
examples.code:
from hypernix.workshop import FrameworkConfig, WorkshopFramework

framework = WorkshopFramework(FrameworkConfig(vocab_size=32000))
model = framework.build().to("cuda")
# ... train model ...
framework.save("./checkpoint")

examples.title: Call a T1 API server
examples.description: The bundled SDK exposes typed helpers and a raw escape hatch for newer endpoints.
examples.code:
from hypernix.t1sdk import T1Client

client = T1Client("https://t1.example.com", credential="YOUR_T1_KEY")
print(client.health())
print(client.whoami())
models = client.list_models()
print([m.model_id for m in models])
# New endpoint not wrapped by this SDK release:
print(client.call("GET", "/status"))
